pr_title: Fix typed arrays not working with concatenation operator `+`
pr_body:
This fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/72948 allowing concatenation of typed arrays and maintaining the type information. Includes a test case as well.

*Bugsquad edit:*
- Fixes #72948
- Fixes #72590
pr_comments:
How does it work with this?

```gdscript
var a: Array[int] = [1, 2, 3]
var b: Array[String] = ["one", "two", "three"]
print(a + b)
```

I think the sum type should be the narrowest type, including type a and type b, and not just the type of the first array? Or maybe it should cause an error?

> How does it work with this?
> 
> ```gdscript
> var a: Array[int] = [1, 2, 3]
> var b: Array[String] = ["one", "two", "three"]
> print(a + b)
> ```
> 
> I think the sum type should be the narrowest type, including type a and type b, and not just the type of the first array? Or maybe it should cause an error?

This would likely result in an error currently. It wouldn't reach the concatenating portion of the code.
I think once `_add_arrays` is reached the types of both arrays were already determined to be identical. Perhaps adding some `CHECK` code to make that more clear but it does seem like the expectation. Open to ideas though. 

In the example the narrowest type would be `Varant`? It might be worth it to be able to write code like:
```gdscript
var node2ds : Array[Node2D] = [ ... ]
var node3ds : Array[Node3D] = [ ... ]
var nodes : Array[Node] = node2ds + node3ds
```

~Thinking about it more, perhaps adding the additional feature pushes this into 4.x territory. I think just focusing on this bug fix for now and open a separate issue for the narrowest type for a potential 4.x release.~ Actually, it does turn out that this allows the above example to run and the concatenation of `node2ds + node3ds` results in a `Array[Node2D]` since that was the left operator.

I took another look after understanding @dalexeev concern. Now the implementation is a bit more involved but covers more use-cases. Hopefully it's still in scope of 4.0. I feel pretty confident with because the tests pretty much cover all the functionality of mixing 2 types together. Feedback is appreciated!

> I feel pretty confident with because the tests pretty much cover all the functionality of mixing 2 types together

I don't see explicit tests for untyped arrays (though maybe some existing tests cover it)? That's my main concern with this change, fixing the obviously broken behavior for typed arrays makes sense but we shouldn't take any risk with untyped arrays at this late stage.

This one is problematic one.

I can approve of `Array[T] + Array[T] = Array[T]` but any other mixing should result in untyped array:
```gdscript
var nodes: Array[Node] = node2ds + node3ds # will work
var objects: Array[Object] = node2ds + node3ds # will fail
```

Trying to guess typed array element type will complicate and slow down things.

So in my opinion, there should no new `mix` method, addition to `_add_arrays` can be simple:
```cpp
if (array_a.is_typed() && array_a.is_same_typed(array_b)) {
  sum.set_typed(array_a.get_typed_builtin(), array_a.get_typed_class_name(), array_a.get_typed_script());
}
```

And ideally in analyzer [there](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/6f64349bfe42b795a6c50e9c2093d38e7a992e7a/modules/gdscript/gdscript_analyzer.cpp#L2602) should be added handling of case with `Array[T] + Array[T]` so that the result is typed as `Array[T]` and not as an untyped one.

> This one is problematic one.

Okay, then let's give it a bit more time to develop and give you guys a bit more time to discuss it. We can cherry-pick the final solution into 4.0.x if it's safe enough.

Adjusted the PR.
* Removed the mixing behavior, keeping it simple and only adding types if both arrays match.
* Enhanced the analyzer code as well to return the proper type, works similar to the `_add_arrays` function, and now the editor shows the lines as "safe".

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1059099/220180612-65c969df-0db2-4be5-81a2-bf54b9ac8558.png)

Superb. 

The other place worth updating is [`type_from_variant`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/9c960a8c2494eb826a557a7ffc96dd4547f9d31e/modules/gdscript/gdscript_analyzer.cpp#L4407) this will be used when two constant arrays combined together to get a datatype for result value typing. Right now it will be resolved to an untyped array.

One thing that you may stumble upon in tests - do not use empty constant typed arrays, there is an unresolved issue with how constants are stored.

Updated with `hard_operation` and now concatenating `const` arrays results in green-lines

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1059099/220200802-9f5bf7a7-8b79-4a2f-82eb-994b2cce4c24.png)
Looks good, except that the test does not match the code style (extra parentheses and spaces).

> Looks good, except that the test does not match the code style (extra parentheses and spaces).

I took a look at some other tests and update mine to be closer in consistency :)
@akien-mga @YuriSizov We should maybe wait for @vnen input as this affects core. But I think everything is alright.

issue_context.title: Typed arrays aren't working with +=
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

v4.0.rc1.official [8843d9ad3]

### System information

Lubuntu

### Issue description

You can't use + or += to mutate typed arrays.

It seems to be not correctly getting the type information from the second operand.

An erudite poster on the discord puts it differently:
> it's more like operator + doesn't retain Array typing
> the syntax for Array Concatenation via operators, but the idea gets across i think


The error you see is:
```Trying to assign an array of type "Array" to a variable of type "Array[int]".```


### Steps to reproduce

```
	var Alice: Array[int] = [1,2,3]
	var Bob: Array[int] = [4,5,6]
	Alice += Bob
```
This will crash with the above error message.

### Minimal reproduction project

[plus_syntax_broken_demo_project.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/10694514/plus_syntax_broken_demo_project.zip)
comments:
Specifically - the `operator +` as the docs describe returns a `Variant` Array
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/164616/217752655-f576780e-708e-438a-8543-d81e665fd1f2.png)

when you do (in this example) Alice + Bob, the returned array loses the typing - going from `Array[int]` to just `Array`

`append_array()` works to concatenate the same typed arrays, but the operator itself can't seem to maintain the typing

```
Alice = Alice + Bob   # fails
Alice += Bob          # fails
Alice.append_array(Bob)  #succeeds
```

I see the same issue when initializing arrays like:
```gdscript
var membervar: Array[ClassDefinedElseWhere] = Array()
```

It seems like this is a more general issue.

@esarver This is not the same issue. You are trying to assign an untyped array to a typed property, which is not possible due to ambiguous behavior. You need to use the assign method of the array if you want to convert your value to the typed array.

If you only want to initialize your property, an array literal should work, `[]`.

Also it compares the value with itself...

Do we need to check `array_b.is_typed()`?
Apologies for the drive by comment... :^) Testing a github action PR review bot and was using your PR as an example.

Technically I don't even think `array_a.is_typed()` needs to be checked. `is_same_typed` might just be enough because if they are both untyped then `set_typed` pretty much acts like a no-op. I guess it can be a bit expensive to call `set_typed` just to set no type though so it helps optimize that use-case.

To answer your question, checking if `array_b.is_typed()` would be redundant. If `array_a.is_typed()` and `array_a.is_same_typed(array_b)` then it can be safe to assume `array_b.is_typed()`.
